I have farmed beans for many years, and I know they do not need chemical fertilizer because they pull nitrogen from the air into the soil themselves. I will spread cow manure on this quarter-hectare plot and plant the local seeds I saved from last season's harvest, since they grow well here and cost me nothing. My family will handle the weeding and daily work by hand when the rains come, but I will hire three young men for two days each to help with the heavy land preparation and harvesting, as my strength is not what it used to be. We have no irrigation here, so we plant when the rains begin and trust in what the soil gives us.
